w10_T4_005570: On Saturday morning Maya counted 159 seashells in her collection box. Before lunch she sold 97 of them at the beach market. In the afternoon she split what was left into 2 equal piles, kept half of them in the box and gave the other pile to her cousin. Her friend Ravi keeps his own shells in a tin, and all day his tin held fewer shells than Maya's box. That evening Maya picked up 14 more shells on the sand and dropped them into her box. Just before bed she handed 28 shells from the box to her little brother. How many seashells are in Maya's box now?
w10_T4_005572: A hardware depot took in 234 crates of bolts on Monday morning. A late truck brought 3 more crates the same evening, and they were stored with the others. Each crate in the depot holds 8 sealed boxes. Every sealed box contains 6 bolts. A clerk then swept up 10 loose bolts from the floor and added them to the depot's stock. How many bolts does the depot have altogether?
w10_T4_005573: A nursery started the week with 68 seed trays. 31 of the trays were crushed in a storm and thrown away. Each remaining tray holds 5 rows of soil, and every row holds 5 seedlings. The nursery divided all of those seedlings equally among 5 greenhouses, and the manager then took charge of just one greenhouse. A neighbour donated 37 more seedlings to that greenhouse, and later 160 seedlings from it were sold to a landscaping firm. The nursery also keeps a dozen watering cans by the door. How many seedlings are left in that greenhouse?
w10_T4_005574: A school drama club printed 189 tickets for each of its 4 evening performances. On the first night a volunteer printed 26 extra tickets by hand, and 54 more were added the next morning. A parent then donated 29 additional tickets to the same pile. The whole pile was split evenly among 5 ticket sellers, and Priya took one share for herself. Priya later got 22 unsold tickets back from a friend. The club keeps a dozen spare programmes in the office cupboard, and the hall itself has 320 seats. How many tickets does Priya have now?
w10_T4_005578: Nadia runs a school bookshop. She began the term with 198 packs of pencils on her shelf. A large delivery made the number of packs on that shelf 2 times what it had been. Each pack holds 7 pencils, and she emptied every pack into one big bin. Over the term students bought 2271 pencils from the bin, and her colleague Tomas, who sold fewer pencils than Nadia did, took 6 pencils out of it for the art room. How many pencils are left in the bin?
w10_T4_005579: A librarian named Ana set up a new reading room. In the morning she placed 71 novels on a display shelf, then added 20 more from a donation crate and 16 that readers had returned. Every shelf in the building was then stocked with exactly that many novels. Each room in the building holds 2 such shelves, and the building has 9 rooms. Her colleague Dev stocked fewer novels than Ana did at his own branch. The library is open 8 hours a day, though the staff record their shifts in minutes rather than hours. How many novels are on the shelves in the building?
w10_T4_005581: A market stall keeps its takings in a coin tin, counting everything in cents and turning the cents into dollars only at closing time. At the start of Saturday morning the tin held 211 cents. A customer added 7 cents in change during the first hour, and then 209 cents were taken out to pay a delivery boy. Around midday a passer-by dropped 27 cents into the tin, and in the early afternoon a sale brought in 46 cents. In the evening the stallholder removed 41 cents to buy a bread roll. How many cents are in the tin at the end of the day?
w10_T4_005586: A dairy records all of its volumes in millilitres, although the labels it prints show litres. On Monday each of the dairy's 6 vans was loaded with 217 crates of milk, and every crate holds 7 bottles. That morning 3402 bottles were sold at the market. A shop returned 65 unopened bottles to the vans in the afternoon. Later 3941 bottles were dropped off at schools along the route. How many bottles are still on the vans?
w10_T4_005587: On Monday morning Marta had 39 flyers for the school play. Before the first bell she handed out 25 of them. At lunchtime the office reprinted her stack so that she was holding 3 times as many flyers as before. In the afternoon her classmate Jonas, who carried fewer flyers than Marta all day, passed her 76 flyers from his own bundle. Later that afternoon Marta posted 76 flyers to families on the mailing list. In the evening she collected 65 freshly printed flyers from the print shop. How many flyers does Marta have at the end of the day?
w10_T4_005588: Farmer Otto packs his eggs into boxes. On Monday there were 226 boxes in each of his 4 barns. That afternoon he sent 592 boxes to a supermarket. Every box that stayed on the farm holds 6 trays, each tray holds 2 rows, and each row holds 7 eggs. His neighbour Petra keeps fewer boxes on her farm than Otto keeps on his. How many eggs are still on Otto's farm?
w10_T4_005591: Nina sold 49 raffle tickets at 5 dollars each on the first day of the school fair. A local shop then added a 67 dollar donation to that day's takings. Each of the 4 days of the fair brought in exactly the same amount as the first day, so the fair's whole total came to 4 times that figure. The total was shared equally among 4 local charities. One of those charities is run by Carlos, who raised far less than Nina did at his own stall, and it later received a 56 dollar gift and then a 42 dollar gift. The fair also sold 310 hot dogs. How many dollars does Carlos's charity have from all of this?
w10_T4_005593: A grain store began the month with 174 sacks of oats. 160 sacks were sent to a bakery, and another 10 went to a riding stable. Each sack that remained holds 7 kilograms of oats, and the store emptied them all into one bin. A farmer then poured 34 more kilograms into the same bin. The store weighs everything in kilograms even though its old scale is marked in pounds, and a dozen empty sacks are stacked by the door. How many kilograms of oats are in the bin?
w10_T4_005594: A bakery baked 172 loaves in each of its 3 ovens on Friday, and a small extra oven produced another 78 loaves. Every loaf was cut into 3 thick slices for the weekend brunch service, and 1681 of those slices were used for sandwiches. Each slice that was left over was topped with 7 olives and set out on the tasting table. Guests then ate 80 of the olives. The cafe has 24 tables. How many olives are still on the tasting table?
w10_T4_005596: Omar had 26 sheets of coloured card for the craft club, and he used 24 of them for posters. Each sheet that was left was cut into 6 gift tags, and he found another 45 finished tags in a drawer. Every tag was decorated with 9 beads from the club's jar, but during the week 488 of those beads fell off and were swept away. Each bead still on a tag is worth 6 cents at the craft sale. Omar's friend Lena decorated fewer tags than Omar did, and their club meets in room 12. How many cents are Omar's remaining beads worth?
w10_T4_005598: Builder Ines keeps cement in 8 sheds, and each shed holds 227 bags. An inspection found 36 torn bags, which were thrown away. Every bag that passed the inspection was split into 2 smaller sacks so the crew could carry them more easily. A neighbouring site run by Diego, who stores fewer sacks than Ines does, sent over 38 more small sacks. Each small sack weighs 6 kilograms, and the site crane can lift 900 kilograms in one go. How many kilograms of cement does Ines now have?
w10_T4_005599: Dani started the month with 93 stickers in her album. She traded 64 of them away at school. A week later she gave 18 stickers to her cousin. Her aunt then sent her a packet holding 28 new stickers, which she pressed into the album. Before the holidays she used 19 stickers to decorate a birthday card. The album has 40 pages. How many stickers are in Dani's album now?
w10_T4_005602: A school film club records all of its running times in minutes and converts them into hours only for the printed programme. The club came back from a trip with 164 minutes of footage, which was split equally between its 2 editors, Ben and Sara, so that each of them started with a share of the same length. Ben cut 76 minutes of shaky material out of his share. He then removed another 3 minutes of silence. Finally he added 70 minutes of interviews to what was left. How many minutes long is Ben's film now?
w10_T4_005604: A chocolate workshop had 110 boxes in its store on Monday, and a delivery on Tuesday made the number of boxes 2 times as large. On Wednesday 168 boxes were shipped to a supermarket. Each box left in the store holds 7 packets, every packet holds 4 bars, and every bar snaps into 2 pieces. Kofi, who runs the workshop, keeps more boxes in store than his rival Amara does. How many pieces of chocolate are in the store?
w10_T4_005607: On Monday morning a juice bar received 62 sacks of oranges, and each sack held 4 baskets. Every basket in those sacks held 3 oranges. By the afternoon a second delivery had doubled the number of oranges in the shop. That evening the owner divided all of the oranges equally among the 3 branches of her business. The next morning the manager of one branch packed that branch's oranges into 4 equal crates and sent a single crate to a school. How many oranges are in the crate that went to the school?
w10_T4_005614: On Monday morning the school library trolley held 128 books. Before lunch Aisha wheeled in 36 books that had been returned over the weekend. In the early afternoon she added 20 books from the reading room, and just before the last bell a teacher put 7 more on the trolley. In the evening the caretaker shelved 144 of the books from the trolley. Aisha handled more books that day than her colleague Mark did. How many books are still on the trolley?
w10_T4_005616: A community kitchen baked 228 bread rolls for a street party. 171 rolls were eaten during the afternoon. A neighbour brought 31 more rolls from her own oven, and a bakery donated 20 more. All of the rolls left on the table were packed equally into 3 boxes for the night shelter. Sofia carried more boxes out to the van than Marco did. How many rolls does one of those boxes hold?
w10_T4_005621: Hana values her stamp collection in cents and works the amount out in dollars only at the end of the year. She owns 235 stamps, but 9 of them are torn and worth nothing, so she set those aside. Every one of her remaining stamps is valued at 5 cents by the collectors club. Her uncle then gave her a club voucher worth 70 cents, and she found another voucher worth 75 cents in a drawer. Her cousin Ivan owns fewer stamps than Hana does, and his album has 48 pages. How many cents are Hana's stamps and vouchers worth in total?
w10_T4_005624: Mrs Patel bought 19 tomato seedlings for her balcony. She gave 17 of them to the community garden. The 2 seedlings she kept were shared equally between 2 identical pots, and she watched only the pot on the left. By July the plant in that pot had grown 3 tomatoes. She picked 2 of them for a salad. The balcony gets 6 hours of sun a day. How many tomatoes are still on that plant?
w10_T4_005625: A party shop had 105 packets of balloons on the shelf. 76 packets were bought for a wedding, and 2 more were ruined by a leak in the roof. Each packet still on the shelf contains 8 balloons, and the owner emptied them all into one bin. A supplier dropped 14 loose balloons into the same bin. A children's party then used 97 balloons from the bin. The shop has 3 other branches. How many balloons are left in the bin?
w10_T4_005634: A school store began September with 165 boxes of crayons, and a delivery brought 33 more. The whole stock was shared equally between the school's 2 buildings, and the art teacher looked after the share in the main building. Parents later donated 76 boxes to that building, and 122 boxes were handed out to classrooms. Another 50 boxes were found to be damp and thrown away. Each box that remains holds 6 crayons, and the school has 480 pupils. How many crayons are left in the main building?
